newsitem.title: UK: Malaysia to guarantee funds for Bakun dam - paper.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to guarantee funds for Bakun dam - paper.

text.p: Malaysia has agreed to guarantee the financing of its $5.4 billion Bakun dam project, according to lead contractor ABB Asea Brown Boveri, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
The British newspaper said it was quoting ABB's chief executive Goran Lindahl, who spoke on Wednesday after meetings with Malaysia's Prime Minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his cabinet.

The Financial Times said Lindahl's comments would help reassure financial markets in advance of Malaysia's planned share flotation of Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp (BHC), the holding firm for the project.
It said Lindahl also confirmed work on the site in Sarawak province on Borneo island had been delayed for a few weeks because of problems building tunnels to divert the river.

Lindahl was reported as saying Dong Ah Construction, the South Korean firm building the three 1.5 km diversion tunnels, had suffered a rockfall on one tunnel but this was now completed and the other two would be ready in five to seven weeks.

ABB could start work on the main site only once the river was diverted. The original plan envisaged the river's diversion in either autumn 1997 or May 1998 but Lindahl said it was still likely that it would be diverted this year, the newspaper said.
